results.title: Dartmouth
results.creator_credit: David Morgan, John Richardson and Kestrel Film Productions
results.brief_description: Dartmouth Dam, on the Mitta Mitta River in Victoria, has been designed to manage the waters of the River Murray for irrigation and urban needs. This film tells the story of the making of Dartmouth Dam including the study of plant and animal life. Reminiscences about the old Dartmouth township, and plans for the new town of Dartmouth. Narrated by Simon Chilvers.

results.title: The Way of the Birds Storyboarding
results.credit_line: ACMI Collection, Sarah Watt Collection, Gift of the Watt-McInnes Family
results.brief_description:
Sarah Watt’s The Way of the Birds (2000) follows Maisie, a young girl whose fascination with birds transforms the way she sees the world. Like Watt herself, Maisie uses drawing to imagine places beyond everyday life, inviting us to see the world from new perspectives.
Trained as a fine artist, Watt made storyboarding central to her creative process. She used sketches to test ideas, shape emotion and gradually transform drawings into moving images. The storyboards, sketches and film stills on display trace that journey, revealing how imagined worlds first take shape on the page before coming to life on screen.
An award-winning Australian director, writer and animator, Watt embraced the expressive possibilities of drawing. Her hand-drawn films carry the warmth and immediacy of the artist’s hand, reminding us that animation is not simply about movement, but about transforming the way we see the world.

constellations_primary.name: Drawn worlds
constellations_primary.description: This Constellation follows artists who use animation to transform how we see the world. Moving between childhood imagination, fantasy and everyday life, these works show how drawings, silhouettes and sculpted figures can carry emotion and bring imagined worlds to life.
